title: Mechanisms of thyroid hormone action
funder: This work was supported by Veterans Affairs Merit Review Funds and NIH grant R01 CA89364.
authorConflicts: The author has declared that no conflict of interest exists.
result: Review. Thyroid hormone is synthesised in thyroid follicles by iodination of tyrosine residues in thyroglobulin; TSH, secreted by the anterior pituitary in response to feedback from circulating thyroid hormone, acts on the TSH receptor of follicular cells and regulates iodide uptake by the sodium/iodide symporter. T4 is a prohormone activated to T3; humans derive circulating T3 primarily from type 2 deiodinase and rodents from type 1; type 3 deiodinase inactivates T4 to reverse T3; selenium is required by all three deiodinases. Unliganded thyroid hormone receptor heterodimerises with RXR, binds a thyroid hormone response element and then a corepressor such as NCoR or SMRT; T3 binding disrupts corepressor binding and promotes coactivator binding. TR-beta mediates thyroid hormone feedback to TRH and TSH; resistance to thyroid hormone, caused by TR-beta mutations, features elevated circulating thyroid hormone and nonsuppressed serum TSH.
